messages:
maria-support: FYI escalation from Acme — they see intermittent 500s on the /v1/generate endpoint. Customer provided a request_id: req_9a8b7c6d. Asking if we can pull server logs and advise. They included a curl they ran.

ben-sre: Can you paste the exact request_id string and the approximate time? Also need the region and model they hit (we have some cross-region routing oddities).

maria-support: Request_id is req_9a8b7c6d, reported around 2026-03-15T18:22:10Z. They called hosted-prod us-west2, model redwood-v2-large. Customer curl (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-large","input":"summarize...","request_id":"req_9a8b7c6d"}' 
  --max-time 30 --verbose
```

ben-sre: thanks. I'll run the KQL hunt across ingest and cold archives. Quick KQL I use to find server-side traces by request_id or trace id:
```
// search by request_id across services
message:*req_9a8b7c6d* or properties.request_id: "req_9a8b7c6d"
| where timestamp >= datetime(2026-03-15T18:00:00Z) and timestamp <= datetime(2026-03-15T19:00:00Z)
| sort by timestamp asc
```
If you have a trace id, also search traces.service and x-request-id headers.

alex-eng: note — logs for that shard rotate to cold after 21 days for hosted-prod. If the customer timestamp is within retention we can find full logs; if older, we may need an archive export. For archive requests open a ticket to infra-archives and include request_id + time window.

tara-customer: We ran this yesterday so it's within 24 hours. We can share full curl and verbose output, plus the X-Request-ID header we saw. We also saw a tiny spike in latency just before failure.

ben-sre: Good. Two immediate asks for repro bundle: 1) full verbose curl output (--verbose) including response headers 2) browser/network HAR or server-side logs if available 3) if they can reproduce, collect a debug bundle using our helper:
```
curl -sS https://internal.redwood.tools/debug-bundle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <support-token>" \
  -F "request_id=req_9a8b7c6d" \
  -F "timestamp=2026-03-15T18:22:10Z"
```
We don't need secrets, just headers, timing, and the raw response bodies (redact keys).

support-bot: Auto note — hosted-prod retention: hot logs 7 days, warm 14 days, cold archive 60 days. Archive export turnaround ~24-72 hrs depending on size. See https://redwood.ai/docs/ops/log-retention

maria-support: I'll ask customer to attach the verbose curl output & HAR. Also requesting permission to fetch their debug bundle (they can upload to the ticket or share a signed link).

ben-sre: Once we have the bundle I'll run the KQL above across the edge, gateway, and model-worker indices. If request_id absent in model-worker logs we fallback to searching by connection_id / peer ip. Also keep an eye for the exact error token: 500: upstream reset / 500: model OOM / 502 gateway. Each has different handoff path.

alex-eng: If we find model-worker 500s that align, we'll check kernel OOM counters and GPU host metrics for that time window. If it's a transient routing N: I'll suggest a canary config change to the routing policy.

maria-support: Customer uploaded the verbose output to ticket INC-54812 and posted a signed link to the debug bundle. Sending link in DM to ben-sre.

ben-sre: Got it. Starting log hunt now. Will paste exact queries and matching log snippets here when I have them. If nothing turns up I will escalate to infra-archives for a cold fetch. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Thanks — I'll update the customer that we're on it and asking them to hold for 24-48 hrs while we complete the pull and analysis.

ben-sre: quick note for audit: include the request_id in the archive ticket and set priority=customer-impact. Also cc: alex-eng for model-worker checks.

maria-support: Done. Closing loop with customer that we have the artifacts and infra hunt in progress.
